claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/.
The post at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration from CDK to Pulumi.
SST was originally built on AWS CDK, which lets developers define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK is AWS-only, whereas Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP and on-prem; Pulumi supports any programming language while CDK supports only TypeScript and Python.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK/CloudFormation, and once stable will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running sst deploy requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account.
Nitric and Defang also run application deployments through the Pulumi engine.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, supporting AWS and more than 150 other providers.
Through 2023 SST was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'
SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says that on sst deploy, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine which calls the bridged Terraform provider, making AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says the imports from Pulumi mean the whole deployment process is built on Pulumi.
SST's platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, @pulumi/aws, @pulumi/cloudflare, @pulumi/command, @pulumi/docker-build, @pulumi/random, @pulumi/tls and @pulumiverse/vercel.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state that 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs pulumi up.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed in the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package had about 796,000 weekly downloads (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has more GitHub stars than SST.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The team's attention on opencode has not changed SST's release cadence.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components exist as Pulumi offerings usable alongside the engine SST runs on.
Linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
